{"success": true, "data": {"stdout": """"Noise-aware collision-shaping loss for GeoSafe-VLA.

Loss components:
  L_FM  : flow-matching MSE (unchanged from openpi)
  L_SDF : MSE between SDF head predictions and ground-truth distances
  L_col : ReLU(margin - sdf_pred) collision penalty, suppressed at high noise

Total: L = L_FM + lambda_sdf * L_SDF + lambda_col * w(t) * L_col

openpi flow-matching convention:
  x_t = t * noise + (1-t) * actions   =>  t=0 clean, t=1 pure noise
  Tweedie estimate: x0_hat = x_t - t * v_pred

Noise-aware weight (adapted for openpi convention where large t = more noise):
  w(t) = sigmoid(alpha * (t0 - t))
    t << t0  =>  w ~ 1  (low noise, penalty active)
    t >> t0  =>  w ~ 0  (high noise, penalty suppressed)
"""

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def compute_sdf_losses(
    sdf_pred: torch.Tensor,
    sdf_gt: torch.Tensor,
    sdf_valid: torch.Tensor,
    flow_time: torch.Tensor,
    collision_threshold: float = 0.02,
    noise_t0: float = 0.5,
    noise_alpha: float = 10.0,
) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
    """Compute SDF regression and collision-shaping losses.

    Args:
        sdf_pred: [B, H] predicted SDF distances from SDF head.
        sdf_gt: [B, H] ground-truth SDF distances.
        sdf_valid: [B] bool mask -- True where SDF labels exist.
        flow_time: [B] flow-matching timesteps (0=clean, 1=noise).
        collision_threshold: safety margin in meters (default 0.02 = 2cm).
        noise_t0: sigmoid center for noise-aware weighting.
        noise_alpha: sigmoid steepness.

    Returns:
        dict with keys 'sdf_loss', 'collision_loss', 'collision_rate'.
        All values are scalar tensors (already reduced).
    """
    device = sdf_pred.device
    zeros = torch.tensor(0.0, device=device)

    if not sdf_valid.any():
        return {"sdf_loss": zeros, "collision_loss": zeros, "collision_rate": zeros}

    valid_pred = sdf_pred[sdf_valid]       # [N, H]
    valid_gt = sdf_gt[sdf_valid]           # [N, H]
    valid_time = flow_time[sdf_valid]      # [N]

    # L_SDF: per-timestep MSE
    sdf_loss = F.mse_loss(valid_pred, valid_gt)

    # L_col: ReLU collision penalty weighted by noise level
    collision_penalty = F.relu(collision_threshold - valid_pred)  # [N, H]
    # w(t) -> 1 when t < t0 (clean), -> 0 when t > t0 (noisy)
    w_t = torch.sigmoid(noise_alpha * (noise_t0 - valid_time))   # [N]
    collision_loss = (w_t[:, None] * collision_penalty).mean()

    # Logging metric: fraction of GT timesteps inside the margin
    collision_rate = (valid_gt < collision_threshold).float().mean()

    return {
        "sdf_loss": sdf_loss,
        "collision_loss": collision_loss,
        "collision_rate": collision_rate,
    }

    title: "GLaD: Geometric Latent Distillation for Vision-Language-Action Models"
    authors: "Minghao Guo, Meng Cao, Jiachen Tao et al."
    year: 2025
    venue: arXiv
    role: direct-competitor
    category: geometric-distillation-vla
    relevance: >
      Distills 3D geometric priors (from VGGT) into VLA's LLM hidden states during pretraining.
      Closest to our guidance internalization paradigm but targets general spatial reasoning,
      not collision safety — no SDF or collision-shaping loss.
    key_findings: >
      Aligns LLM hidden states (not just vision encoder) with frozen geometry-aware ViT features.
      Achieves 94.1% average success on LIBERO, outperforming UniVLA (92.5%).
      Demonstrates that geometric distillation into deeper model layers is more effective than
      vision-encoder-only alignment.

  omniguide:
    arxiv_id: "2603.10052"
    title: "OmniGuide: Universal Guidance Fields for Enhancing Generalist Robot Policies"
    authors: "Yunzhou Song, Long Le, Yong-Hyun Park et al."
    year: 2026
    venue: arXiv
    role: direct-competitor
    category: inference-time-guidance-vla
    relevance: >
      Uses differentiable SDF-based energy fields to guide flow-matching VLAs at inference time.
      Demonstrates SDF gradients dramatically improve collision avoidance (7.0% → 93.5% CAR on RoboCasa)
      but adds ~2x latency. GeoSafe-VLA internalizes this SDF guidance into weights during training
      for zero inference overhead.
    key_findings: >
      Differentiable energy functions (SDF collision repulsion, semantic attractors) guide π₀.₅/GR00T
      at inference via backprop through differentiable kinematics into denoising loop.
      Training-free but ~2x latency. Handles novel obstacles naturally via explicit SDF computation.
      Susceptible to potential field local minima in dense clutter.

  aegis_vlsa:
    arxiv_id: "2512.11891"
    title: "VLSA: Vision-Language-Action Models with Plug-and-Play Safety Constraint Layer"
    authors: "Songqiao Hu, Zeyi Liu, Shuang Liu et al."
    year: 2025
    venue: arXiv
    role: direct-competitor
    category: post-hoc-safety-vla
    relevance: >
      Current SafeLIBERO SOTA. Uses CBF-based post-hoc correction (AEGIS layer) for VLA safety.
      Explicitly acknowledges OOD trajectory drift when corrections push actions out of training
      distribution. GeoSafe-VLA's internalized approach avoids this OOD drift by generating
      inherently safe in-distribution actions.
    key_findings: >
      Proposes AEGIS plug-and-play safety constraint layer using control barrier functions.
      Constructs SafeLIBERO benchmark (32 scenarios, 1600 episodes). Achieves 68.13% TSR,
      77.85% CAR on π₀.₅. Improves collision avoidance 59.16% but acknowledges OOD drift risk.

  safevla:
    arxiv_id: "2503.03480"
    title: "SafeVLA: Towards Safety Alignment of Vision-Language-Action Model via Constrained Learning"
    authors: "Borong Zhang, Yuhao Zhang, Jiaming Ji et al."
    year: 2025
    venue: NeurIPS 2025 (Spotlight)
    role: direct-competitor
    category: rl-safety-vla
    relevance: >
      Uses constrained RL fine-tuning for VLA safety alignment. Reduces safety violation cost
      by 83.58%. Complementary approach to ours — RL-based vs. geometric-based. Must compare
      and clarify that geometric internalization provides explicit spatial grounding that abstract
      cost functions lack.
    key_findings: >
      Proposes integrated safety approach: modeling safety requirements, eliciting unsafe behaviors,
      constraining VLA via safe RL, and targeted evaluation. Reduces cumulative safety cost 83.58%
      and upper bound of unsafe behaviors to 1/35 of SOTA.

  safediffuser:
    arxiv_id: "2306.00148"
    title: "SafeDiffuser: Safe Planning with Diffusion Probabilistic Models"
    authors: "Wei Xiao, Tsun-Hsuan Wang, Chuang Gan, Daniela Rus"
    year: 2023
    venue: ICLR 2025
    role: direct-competitor
    category: safe-diffusion-planning
    relevance: >
      Embeds CBF-based safety constraints into diffusion denoising procedure for safe planning.
      Foundational work on integrating safety into diffusion-based generation. Differs from
      GeoSafe-VLA: operates on planning (not VLA actions), uses CBF invariance (not SDF
      internalization), and retains constraints at inference.
    key_findings: >
      Proposes finite-time diffusion invariance using control barrier functions embedded in
      denoising. Tested on maze generation, legged locomotion, and 3D manipulation. Maintains
      generalization while providing safety guarantees.

  scpo:
    arxiv_id: "2306.12594"
    title: "State-wise Constrained Policy Optimization"
    authors: "Weiye Zhao, Rui Chen, Yifan Sun et al."
    year: 2024
    venue: arXiv
    role: direct-competitor
    category: safe-robot-learning
    relevance: >
      Constrained RL approach enforcing state-wise (per-timestep) safety constraints via SCMDP
      formulation. Uses explicit constraint optimization at policy level, whereas GeoSafe-VLA
      internalizes SDF collision geometry into VLA weights during training — no constraint
      solver needed at inference.
    key_findings: >
      First general-purpose policy search algorithm for state-wise constrained RL. Introduces
      Maximum Markov Decision Process framework with provable bounds on worst-case safety
      violation. Significantly outperforms cumulative-constraint CMDP baselines on high-dimensional
      robotics tasks including autonomous driving and robot manipulation.

  cofree_vla:
    arxiv_id: "2601.21712"
    title: "CoFreeVLA: Collision-Free Dual-Arm Manipulation via VLA Model and Risk Estimation"
    authors: "(Jan 2026)"
    year: 2026
    venue: arXiv
    role: direct-competitor
    category: risk-gating-vla
    relevance: >
      Semi-internalized approach: trains risk estimator to gate unsafe dual-arm actions.
      Binary halt/continue rather than continuous geometric shaping. Different from GeoSafe-VLA's
      continuous SDF-based collision shaping.
    key_findings: >
      Trains risk estimator for dual-arm collision avoidance using binary gating mechanism.
      Semi-internalized but lacks continuous geometric reasoning.

  pi0:

  pi05:

    venue: arXiv

      for GeoSafe-VLA fine-tuning via openpi codebase. Co-training on heterogeneous tasks
      enables broad generalization — our collision awareness is added on top.
    key_findings: >
      Uses co-training on heterogeneous tasks (multiple robots, semantic prediction, web data)
      for open-world generalization. Tested in unfamiliar real homes. Open-source weights and
      fine-tuning code available via openpi.

  occvla:
    arxiv_id: "2509.05578"
    title: "OccVLA: Vision-Language-Action Model with Implicit 3D Occupancy Supervision"
    authors: "Ruixun Liu, Lingyu Kong, Derun Li, Hang Zhao"
    year: 2025
    venue: arXiv
    role: method-component
    category: occupancy-vla
    relevance: >
      Core inspiration: proves occupancy prediction can serve as VLA's implicit reasoning process,
      skippable at inference (zero overhead). But targets autonomous driving. GeoSafe-VLA adapts
      the 'train-with, infer-without' paradigm to manipulation safety with SDF instead of
      occupancy voxels.
    key_findings: >
      Treats dense 3D occupancy as both predictive output and supervisory signal for driving VLA.
      Learns spatial structure from 2D vision only. Occupancy prediction serves as implicit
      reasoning, optionally skippable at inference. SOTA on nuScenes trajectory planning.

  spatial_forcing:
    arxiv_id: "2510.12276"
    title: "Spatial Forcing: Implicit Spatial Representation Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Model"
    authors: "Fuhao Li, Wenxuan Song, Han Zhao et al."
    year: 2025
    venue: ICLR 2026
    role: method-component
    category: spatial-alignment-vla

      3.8× training acceleration. Targets spatial alignment, not collision avoidance.

{"success": true, "data": {"path": "/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0513_4/projects/geosafe_vla/literature_map.yaml", "content": "# GeoSafe-VLA Literature Map
# Generated: 2026-05-20

papers:

  # ── Direct Competitors ──────────────────────────────────────────────

  glad:
    arxiv_id: "2512.09619"
    title: "GLaD: Geometric Latent Distillation for Vision-Language-Action Models"
    authors: "Minghao Guo, Meng Cao, Jiachen Tao et al."
    year: 2025
    venue: arXiv
    role: direct-competitor
    category: geometric-distillation-vla
    relevance: >
      Distills 3D geometric priors (from VGGT) into VLA's LLM hidden states during pretraining.
      Closest to our guidance internalization paradigm but targets general spatial reasoning,
      not collision safety — no SDF or collision-shaping loss.
    key_findings: >
      Aligns LLM hidden states (not just vision encoder) with frozen geometry-aware ViT features.
      Achieves 94.1% average success on LIBERO, outperforming UniVLA (92.5%).
      Demonstrates that geometric distillation into deeper model layers is more effective than
      vision-encoder-only alignment.

  omniguide:
    arxiv_id: "2603.10052"
    title: "OmniGuide: Universal Guidance Fields for Enhancing Generalist Robot Policies"
    authors: "Yunzhou Song, Long Le, Yong-Hyun Park et al."
    year: 2026
    venue: arXiv
    role: direct-competitor
    category: inference-time-guidance-vla
    relevance: >
      Uses differentiable SDF-based energy fields to guide flow-matching VLAs at inference time.
      Demonstrates SDF gradients dramatically improve collision avoidance (7.0% → 93.5% CAR on RoboCasa)
      but adds ~2x latency. GeoSafe-VLA internalizes this SDF guidance into weights during training
      for zero inference overhead.
    key_findings: >
      Differentiable energy functions (SDF collision repulsion, semantic attractors) guide π₀.₅/GR00T
      at inference via backprop through differentiable kinematics into denoising loop.
      Training-free but ~2x latency. Handles novel obstacles naturally via explicit SDF computation.
      Susceptible to potential field local minima in dense clutter.

  aegis_vlsa:
    arxiv_id: "2512.11891"
    title: "VLSA: Vision-Language-Action Models with Plug-and-Play Safety Constraint Layer"
    authors: "Songqiao Hu, Zeyi Liu, Shuang Liu et al."
    year: 2025
    venue: arXiv
    role: direct-competitor
    category: post-hoc-safety-vla
    relevance: >
      Current SafeLIBERO SOTA. Uses CBF-based post-hoc correction (AEGIS layer) for VLA safety.
      Explicitly acknowledges OOD trajectory drift when corrections push actions out of training
      distribution. GeoSafe-VLA's internalized approach avoids this OOD drift by generating
      inherently safe in-distribution actions.
    key_findings: >
      Proposes AEGIS plug-and-play safety constraint layer using control barrier functions.
      Constructs SafeLIBERO benchmark (32 scenarios, 1600 episodes). Achieves 68.13% TSR,
      77.85% CAR on π₀.₅. Improves collision avoidance 59.16% but acknowledges OOD drift risk.

  safevla:
    arxiv_id: "2503.03480"
    title: "SafeVLA: Towards Safety Alignment of Vision-Language-Action Model via Constrained Learning"
    authors: "Borong Zhang, Yuhao Zhang, Jiaming Ji et al."
    year: 2025
    venue: NeurIPS 2025 (Spotlight)
    role: direct-competitor
    category: rl-safety-vla
    relevance: >
      Uses constrained RL fine-tuning for VLA safety alignment. Reduces safety violation cost
      by 83.58%. Complementary approach to ours — RL-based vs. geometric-based. Must compare
      and clarify that geometric internalization provides explicit spatial grounding that abstract
      cost functions lack.
    key_findings: >
      Proposes integrated safety approach: modeling safety requirements, eliciting unsafe behaviors,
      constraining VLA via safe RL, and targeted evaluation. Reduces cumulative safety cost 83.58%
      and upper bound of unsafe behaviors to 1/35 of SOTA.

  safediffuser:
    arxiv_id: "2306.00148"
    title: "SafeDiffuser: Safe Planning with Diffusion Probabilistic Models"
    authors: "Wei Xiao, Tsun-Hsuan Wang, Chuang Gan, Daniela Rus"
    year: 2023
    venue: ICLR 2025
    role: direct-competitor
    category: safe-diffusion-planning
    relevance: >
      Embeds CBF-based safety constraints into diffusion denoising procedure for safe planning.
      Foundational work on integrating safety into diffusion-based generation. Differs from
      GeoSafe-VLA: operates on planning (not VLA actions), uses CBF invariance (not SDF
      internalization), and retains constraints at inference.
    key_findings: >
      Proposes finite-time diffusion invariance using control barrier functions embedded in
      denoising. Tested on maze generation, legged locomotion, and 3D manipulation. Maintains
      generalization while providing safety guarantees.

  scpo:
    arxiv_id: "2306.12594"
    title: "State-wise Constrained Policy Optimization"
    authors: "Weiye Zhao, Rui Chen, Yifan Sun et al."
    year: 2024
    venue: arXiv
    role: direct-competitor
    category: safe-robot-learning
    relevance: >
      Constrained RL approach enforcing state-wise (per-timestep) safety constraints via SCMDP
      formulation. Uses explicit constraint optimization at policy level, whereas GeoSafe-VLA
      internalizes SDF collision geometry into VLA weights during training — no constraint
      solver needed at inference.
    key_findings: >
      First general-purpose policy search algorithm for state-wise constrained RL. Introduces
      Maximum Markov Decision Process framework with provable bounds on worst-case safety
      violation. Significantly outperforms cumulative-constraint CMDP baselines on high-dimensional
      robotics tasks including autonomous driving and robot manipulation.

  cofree_vla:
    arxiv_id: "2601.21712"
    title: "CoFreeVLA: Collision-Free Dual-Arm Manipulation via VLA Model and Risk Estimation"
    authors: "(Jan 2026)"
    year: 2026
    venue: arXiv
    role: direct-competitor
    category: risk-gating-vla
    relevance: >
      Semi-internalized approach: trains risk estimator to gate unsafe dual-arm actions.
      Binary halt/continue rather than continuous geometric shaping. Different from GeoSafe-VLA's
      continuous SDF-based collision shaping.
    key_findings: >
      Trains risk estimator for dual-arm collision avoidance using binary gating mechanism.
      Semi-internalized but lacks continuous geometric reasoning.

  # ── Method Components ───────────────────────────────────────────────

  pi0:
    arxiv_id: "2410.24164"
    title: "π₀: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control"
    authors: "Kevin Black, Noah Brown, Danny Driess et al."
    year: 2024
    venue: arXiv
    role: method-component
    category: base-vla-architecture
    relevance: >
      Base VLA architecture for GeoSafe-VLA. Flow-matching architecture built on PaliGemma VLM,
      pre-trained across 8 robot platforms. Our SDF auxiliary head and collision-shaping loss are
      applied during flow-matching fine-tuning of this architecture.
    key_findings: >
      Novel flow-matching VLA architecture on pre-trained VLM. Pre-trained on 10,000+ hours of
      demonstration data across 7 robot configurations and 68 tasks. Establishes general VLA
      control paradigm enabling zero-shot and fine-tuned deployment.

  pi05:
    arxiv_id: "2504.16054"
    title: "π₀.₅: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization"
    authors: "Kevin Black, Noah Brown, James Darpinian et al."
    year: 2025
    venue: arXiv
    role: method-component
    category: base-vla-architecture
    relevance: >
      Open-source upgraded version of π₀ with open-world generalization. Primary base model
      for GeoSafe-VLA fine-tuning via openpi codebase. Co-training on heterogeneous tasks
      enables broad generalization — our collision awareness is added on top.
    key_findings: >
      Uses co-training on heterogeneous tasks (multiple robots, semantic prediction, web data)
      for open-world generalization. Tested in unfamiliar real homes. Open-source weights and
      fine-tuning code available via openpi.

  occvla:
    arxiv_id: "2509.05578"
    title: "OccVLA: Vision-Language-Action Model with Implicit 3D Occupancy Supervision"
    authors: "Ruixun Liu, Lingyu Kong, Derun Li, Hang Zhao"
    year: 2025
    venue: arXiv
    role: method-component
    category: occupancy-vla
    relevance: >
      Core inspiration: proves occupancy prediction can serve as VLA's implicit reasoning process,
      skippable at inference (zero overhead). But targets autonomous driving. GeoSafe-VLA adapts
      the 'train-with, infer-without' paradigm to manipulation safety with SDF instead of
      occupancy voxels.
    key_findings: >
      Treats dense 3D occupancy as both predictive output and supervisory signal for driving VLA.
      Learns spatial structure from 2D vision only. Occupancy prediction serves as implicit
      reasoning, optionally skippable at inference. SOTA on nuScenes trajectory planning.

  spatial_forcing:
    arxiv_id: "2510.12276"
    title: "Spatial Forcing: Implicit Spatial Representation Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Model"
    authors: "Fuhao Li, Wenxuan Song, Han Zhao et al."
    year: 2025
    venue: ICLR 2026
    role: method-component
    category: spatial-alignment-vla
    relevance: >
      Proves implicit 3D alignment improves VLA spatial reasoning without explicit 3D input.
      Validates the 'train-with-geometry, infer-without' paradigm for spatial precision.
      GeoSafe-VLA specializes the alignment target from general 3D geometry to SDF collision
      geometry.
    key_findings: >
      Aligns VLA intermediate visual embeddings with 3D foundation model representations.
      Plug-and-play (~30 lines of code). SOTA surpassing 2D and 3D VLA baselines.
      3.8× training acceleration. Targets spatial alignment, not collision avoidance.

  cssdf_net:
    arxiv_id: "2603.18669"
    title: "CSSDF-Net: Safe Motion Planning Based on Neural Implicit Representations of Configuration Space Distance Field"
    authors: "Haohua Chen, Yixuan Zhou, Yifan Zhou, Hesheng Wang"
    year: 2026
    venue: arXiv
    role: method-component
    category: neural-sdf-planning
    relevance: >
      Demonstrates neural implicit SDF in configuration space for collision-free motion planning.
      Validates SDF as effective collision representation in joint space — same space where
      GeoSafe-VLA's SDF head operates. Traditional planning, not VLA.
    key_findings: >
      Models continuous differentiable SDF directly in configuration space. Spatial-hashing-based
      data generation enables zero-shot generalization to arbitrary obstacle point sets.
      Integrated into trajectory optimization and MPC for offline/online collision avoidance.

  ngdf:
    arxiv_id: "2211.02647"
    title: "Neural Grasp Distance Fields for Robot Manipulation"
    authors: "Thomas Weng, David Held, Franziska Meier, Mustafa Mukadam"
    year: 2023
    venue: ICRA 2023
    role: method-component
    category: neural-distance-field-manipulation
    relevance: >
      Validates neural distance fields for robot manipulation. Distance field gradients used in
      trajectory optimization for collision avoidance + smoothness. Conceptual ancestor of our
      SDF head approach but in traditional planning, not VLA.
    key_findings: >
      Represents grasps as neural distance fields: 6D pose input, distance to valid grasp manifold
      output. Continuous differentiable field embedded in trajectory optimization. Outperforms
      baselines by 63% execution success. Generalizes to unseen shapes.

  geopredict:
    arxiv_id: "2512.16811"
    title: "GeoPredict: Leveraging Predictive Kinematics and 3D Gaussian Geometry for Precise VLA Manipulation"
    authors: "Jingjing Qian, Boyao Han, Chen Shi et al."
    year: 2025
    venue: arXiv
    role: method-component
    category: geometry-supervision-vla
    relevance: >
      Uses training-time 3D Gaussian geometry supervision dropped at inference for VLA precision.
      Validates 'train-with-geometry, infer-without' paradigm for precision but not safety.
      GeoSafe-VLA extends this paradigm to collision safety.
    key_findings: >
      Augments VLA with predictive kinematic (multi-step 3D keypoint trajectories) and
      3D Gaussian geometry modules. Geometry supervision improves precision without
      inference overhead. Targets manipulation accuracy, not collision avoidance.

  # ── Theoretical Foundations ─────────────────────────────────────────

  guidance_distillation:
    arxiv_id: "2210.03142"
    title: "On Distillation of Guided Diffusion Models"

Based on the search results, here's what I found about CHOMP:

## CHOMP: Covariant Hamiltonian Optimization for Motion Planning

CHOMP is a method for trajectory optimization invariant to reparametrization. The paper was authored by Matthew Zucker, Nathan Ratliff, Anca Dragan, Mikhail Pivtoraiko, Matthew Klingensmith, Christopher Dellin, J. Andrew Bagnell, and Siddhartha Srinivasa and published in August 2013 in the International Journal of Robotics Research, Vol. 32, No. 9, pp. 1164-1193.

### Key Features

CHOMP uses functional gradient techniques to iteratively improve the quality of an initial trajectory, optimizing a functional that trades off between a smoothness and an obstacle avoidance component. CHOMP can be used to locally optimize feasible trajectories, as well as to solve motion planning queries, converging to low-cost trajectories even when initialized with infeasible ones.

It uses Hamiltonian Monte Carlo to alleviate the problem of convergence to high-cost local minima (and for probabilistic completeness), and is capable of respecting hard constraints along the trajectory. The researchers presented extensive experiments with CHOMP on manipulation and locomotion tasks, using 7-DOF manipulators and a rough-terrain quadruped robot.

Based on the search results, I found comprehensive information about the DeepSDF paper:

## DeepSDF: Learning Continuous Signed Distance Functions for Shape Representation

DeepSDF was published by Park, J.J., Florence, P., Straub, J., Newcombe, R. and Lovegrove, S. at the 2019 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) in Long Beach, June 15-20, 2019, pages 165-174.

**Overview:**
DeepSDF is a learned continuous Signed Distance Function (SDF) representation of a class of shapes that enables high quality shape representation, interpolation and completion from partial and noisy 3D input data.

**Technical Approach:**
DeepSDF represents a shape's surface by a continuous volumetric field: the magnitude of a point in the field represents the distance to the surface boundary and the sign indicates whether the region is inside (-) or outside (+) of the shape. DeepSDF represents signed distance functions (SDFs) of shapes via latent code-conditioned feed-forward decoder networks.

**Key Advantage:**
While classical SDFs both in analytical or discretized voxel form typically represent the surface of a single shape, DeepSDF can represent an entire class of shapes.

The paper has been highly influential, with implementations and resources available through the official Facebook Research GitHub repository.

I found comprehensive information about RT-2 (Robotic Transformer 2) from Google DeepMind. Here's what the search reveals:

## Overview

In 2023, Google DeepMind introduced 'RT-2,' a 'Vision-Language-Action' (VLA) model that directly translates visual observations and natural language instructions into robotic commands.

## Key Innovation

While previous robots required separate modules for perception, reasoning, and control, RT-2 uses a single large model that has been pre-trained on billions of words and images from the internet. RT-2 established a "Vision-Language-Action" (VLA) framework by reformulating robotic control as a native translation task within a large-scale multimodal transformer.

## Training Approach

The model was trained simultaneously on two massive datasets: internet-scale vision-language data (containing 10 billion image-text pairs) and specialized robotic trajectory data, with robotic data making up roughly 50% to 66% of the training batches.

## Technical Approach

To fit both natural language responses and robotic actions into the same format, the researchers express the actions as text tokens and incorporate them directly into the training set of the model in the same way as natural language tokens.

## Capabilities

RT-2 shows improved generalisation capabilities and semantic and visual understanding beyond the robotic data it was exposed to.

The arXiv paper is available at arXiv:2307.15818.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about OpenVLA:

## Overview

OpenVLA 7B is an open vision-language-action model trained on 970K robot manipulation episodes from the Open X-Embodiment dataset. The model takes language instructions and camera images as input and generates robot actions.

## Key Publication Details

The paper "OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model" was authored by Moo Jin Kim, Karl Pertsch, Siddharth Karamcheti, Ted Xiao, Ashwin Balakrishna, Suraj Nair, Rafael Rafailov, Ethan Foster, Grace Lam, Pannag Sanketi, Quan Vuong, Thomas Kollar, Benjamin Burchfiel, Russ Tedrake, Dorsa Sadigh, Sergey Levine, Percy Liang, and Chelsea Finn, published on arXiv (arXiv:2406.09246) in 2024.

## Purpose and Motivation

Large policies pretrained on internet-scale vision-language data and diverse robot demonstrations can change how robots learn new skills; however, widespread adoption of VLAs for robotics has been challenging as existing VLAs are largely closed and inaccessible, and prior work fails to explore efficient fine-tuning methods.

## Resources

The project includes released model checkpoints, fine-tuning notebooks, and a PyTorch codebase with built-in support for training VLAs at scale on Open X-Embodiment datasets.

## Flow Matching for Generative Modeling (Lipman et al., 2023)

The paper "Flow Matching for Generative Modeling" was authored by Yaron Lipman, Ricky T. Q. Chen, Heli Ben-Hamu, Maximilian Nickel, and Matt Le, and published at ICLR 2023.

### Key Contribution

The work introduces a new paradigm for generative modeling built on Continuous Normalizing Flows (CNFs), allowing training of CNFs at unprecedented scale. Specifically, Flow Matching (FM) is a simulation-free approach for training CNFs based on regressing vector fields of fixed conditional probability paths.

### Performance and Results

Training CNFs using Flow Matching on ImageNet leads to consistently better performance than alternative diffusion-based methods in terms of both likelihood and sample quality, and allows fast and reliable sample generation using off-the-shelf numerical ODE solvers.

### ArXiv Information

The paper's arXiv identifier is https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.02747

Note that concurrent work including Rectified Flow (Liu et al., 2023) and Stochastic Interpolants (Albergo & Vanden-Eijnden, 2023) were published concurrently at ICLR 2023 with structurally similar contributions under different names.

Training CNFs using Flow Matching on ImageNet leads to consistently better performance than alternative diffusion-based methods in terms of both likelihood and sample quality, and allows fast and reliable sample generation using off-the-shelf numerical ODE solvers.

The paper's arXiv identifier is https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.02747

Note that concurrent work including Rectified Flow (Liu et al., 2023) and Stochastic Interpolants (Albergo & Vanden-Eijnden, 2023) were published concurrently at ICLR 2023 with structurally similar contributions under different names.

## Recent Research on Auxiliary Losses in Robot Learning

Reinforcement Learning via Auxiliary Task Distillation (AuxDistill) is a method for training policies for long-horizon tasks with end-to-end RL that learns auxiliary tasks using a multi-task RL framework and transfers knowledge from these auxiliary tasks to help solve the main task.

Auxiliary tasks help because they are easier to learn with RL than the main task and contain relevant behaviors for the full task. A distillation objective transfers behaviors from relevant auxiliary tasks by encouraging the policy to act consistently between the main and auxiliary tasks for relevant states in the main task.

## Predictive Information as Auxiliary Loss

Predictive information—the mutual information between the past and future—has been shown to be a useful representation learning auxiliary loss for training reinforcement learning agents. Predictive Information QT-Opt (PI-QT-Opt) is a QT-Opt agent augmented with an auxiliary loss that learns representations of the predictive information to solve up to 297 vision-based robot manipulation tasks in simulation and the real world.

### 缺口 1: SDF 经典基础（论文已引 zucker2013chomp 但未入图谱）

```yaml
  chomp:
    arxiv_id: null  # IJRR journal paper, no arXiv
    doi: "10.1177/0278364913488805"
    title: "CHOMP: Covariant Hamiltonian Optimization for Motion Planning"
    authors: "Matthew Zucker, Nathan Ratliff, Anca Dragan, Mihail Pivtoraiko, Matthew Klingensmith, Christopher Dellin, J. Andrew Bagnell, Siddhartha Srinivasa"
    year: 2013
    venue: "IJRR, Vol. 32, No. 9"
    role: theoretical-foundation
    category: sdf-trajectory-optimization
    relevance: >
      Classic gradient-based trajectory optimization using SDF cost fields for collision
      avoidance. Directly cited in our Related Work (zucker2013chomp). Foundational work
      establishing SDF gradients as collision-avoidance signal in trajectory space — GeoSafe-VLA
      internalizes this principle into VLA weights rather than running online optimization.
    key_findings: >
      Functional gradient descent on trajectory cost = smoothness + SDF obstacle cost.
      Hamiltonian Monte Carlo for escaping local minima. Tested on 7-DOF manipulators
      and quadruped locomotion. Establishes SDF as the standard collision representation
      for gradient-based motion planning.
```

### 缺口 2: 神经 SDF 基础

```yaml
  deepsdf:
    arxiv_id: "1901.05103"
    title: "DeepSDF: Learning Continuous Signed Distance Functions for Shape Representation"
    authors: "Jeong Joon Park, Peter Florence, Julian Straub, Richard Newcombe, Steven Lovegrove"
    year: 2019
    venue: CVPR 2019
    role: theoretical-foundation
    category: neural-sdf-representation
    relevance: >
      Foundational work on learning continuous SDF via neural networks. Demonstrates
      that neural networks can represent entire shape classes as continuous distance fields.
      GeoSafe-VLA's SDF head conceptually follows this paradigm — predicting continuous
      distance values from learned features, though our SDF head predicts per-timestep
      distances from VLA hidden states rather than from spatial coordinates.
    key_findings: >
      Latent-code-conditioned feedforward decoder learns continuous SDF for shape classes.
      Enables shape interpolation, completion from partial data, and compact representation.
      4000+ citations. Established neural implicit SDF as a core 3D representation paradigm.
```

### 缺口 3: VLA 开源基线

```yaml
  openvla:
    arxiv_id: "2406.09246"
    title: "OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model"
    authors: "Moo Jin Kim, Karl Pertsch, Siddharth Karamcheti, Ted Xiao et al."
    year: 2024
    venue: arXiv
    role: method-component
    category: open-source-vla
    relevance: >
      First fully open-source VLA (7B params) trained on 970K episodes from Open X-Embodiment.
      Important reference point for VLA fine-tuning methodology. GeoSafe-VLA builds on π₀.₅
      (also open-source) but OpenVLA represents the alternative VLA architecture family —
      discrete action tokenization vs. π₀'s flow-matching continuous actions.
    key_findings: >
      Demonstrates VLA fine-tuning on downstream tasks with parameter-efficient methods.
      Built on Prismatic VLM backbone. Open weights, code, and fine-tuning recipes.
      Establishes reproducible VLA baseline for the community.
```

### 缺口 4: Flow Matching 理论基础

```yaml
  flow_matching:
    arxiv_id: "2210.02747"
    title: "Flow Matching for Generative Modeling"
    authors: "Yaron Lipman, Ricky T. Q. Chen, Heli Ben-Hamu, Maximilian Nickel, Matt Le"
    year: 2023
    venue: ICLR 2023
    role: theoretical-foundation
    category: flow-matching-theory
    relevance: >
      Theoretical foundation for π₀/π₀.₅'s action generation mechanism. Flow matching
      defines the x_t = t*noise + (1-t)*data interpolation and velocity field regression
      that GeoSafe-VLA's noise-aware gating w(t) directly depends on. Understanding this
      is essential for interpreting our collision-shaping loss design.
    key_findings: >
      Simulation-free training of continuous normalizing flows via conditional probability
      path regression. Simpler and more stable than diffusion-based alternatives. Optimal
      transport paths enable faster sampling. Foundation for flow-matching VLAs.
```

### 缺口 5: VLA 先驱

```yaml

    arxiv_id: "2307.15818"
    title: "RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control"

      through π₀.₅ and adds geometric safety as an orthogonal training-time objective.
      Important positioning reference: RT-2 showed VLAs can reason, GeoSafe shows VLAs
      can be made geometrically safe without runtime overhead.
    key_findings: >
      Co-training on 10B image-text pairs + robot data. Actions represented as text tokens.
      Emergent capabilities: object attribute reasoning, multi-step planning from language.
      Established VLA as a viable paradigm for general robot control.
```
